goal: PG-302: one tree view shows every block verdict (rule tree_view_shows_every_block_verdict, known-bad tree_view_hides_a_failing_block)

components.summary: One evaluation engine for tree and single-system files, bounded solve, residual assembly and signal mapping
responsibilities: Use one evaluation engine for tree and single-system files through HierarchicalAuditRunner. Validate inputs and finite solver bounds before residual evaluation Hierarchical run retains reference solving and diagnostics; generated mapping ledgers have no separate review API. For failed observed audits, probe at most 20 observed dependency ancestors for bounded unit factors/offsets, rederive affected native values, and emit hints without editing observations.
Separate numerical optimization success, observed audit and diagnostic limits

Derive intermediate values from connections and bounded one-unknown relations with finite structural value/control provenance; keep producing occurrences separate from independent checks and list unresolved inputs; preserve per-result sources through finite native tuple/dict returns, lexical helpers and fixed numeric parameter tables
Treat connections as physical identities with a tight default residual scale or an explicit positive finite tolerance
Report an observed value without a source signal or unit as a mapping gap
Record stale_when as review conditions; mark mapping stale only from explicit mapping_status stale

Roll child failures into parent verdicts while preserving own scores; compare linked coarse checked relations and report unbuilt refinement targets as planned and resolve built templates without execution; render declared component contracts, ownership and connections without solving
Render one tree view for the declared structure and, when given, the verdicts of an evaluation or a variant run
side_effects: Temporarily chain and restore the current-thread Python trace while collecting partial-snapshot native residual dependencies

responsibilities: Dispatch native commands, list module contracts and render declared model trees or Mermaid without running unrelated owners Expose testfile manifest/check/inspect/diff/snapshot/series; retired dataset and coverage commands are absent. run --json exposes the full diagnostic report. Preflight reviews optionally accept --audit; mapping review is part of hierarchy evaluate. Describe a declared tree as text, full JSON or Mermaid and count observed mappings per block without solving or evaluating; expose mapping-summary counts in observed summaries
Print a compact validation summary with check counts and assumption dispositions, and the full report with --json
hierarchy run, evaluate, compare and variants print the tree view by default and the full report with --json
Write manifest source paths relative to the output manifest directory while preserving stdout-only path behavior
Exit 0 on a passed check, 1 on a checked failure, and 2 when the command cannot run; comparison uses observed audit status
Inspect assumption cards from either a single SystemSpec or the system inside a hierarchical audit
Expose local/subtree verdicts, refinement consistency and per-template status in hierarchy summaries; pass the audit directory for file resolution
Run hierarchy variants with optional fault compositions and observed signature matching; expose masked pairs, next signals and model misses without changing nominal inputs
side_effects: Write explicitly requested native manifest, SI snapshot or series output files
